# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 47 (Bu-Vb Pc47)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc47  
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 47  
**Title (English, from literature):** Accepting an invitation of more than four months  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 47, titled *Catumāsappaccayapavāraṇā* ("Accepting an invitation of more than four months"), is a monastic rule in the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka regulating how Buddhist monks accept invitations from lay supporters for requisites. Under this training rule, a monk who exceeds the specific terms of an invitation when requesting requisites commits an expiation offense (*pācittiya*). In secondary analysis, Ute Hüsken notes this four-month provision (Pāc 47) in connection with the minimum duration monastics spend in a single dwelling place, under which a standing invitation for requisites is ordinarily valid for a period of only up to four months [Hüsken 1997]. Complete translations of the text include an English rendering by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Within the Pāli canon, it corresponds internally to the Pātimokkha rule, the Bhikkhu Parivāra, and the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (Pācittiya 128).
